name: Anthony Towns
cooked:
My view, fwiw:

  • Chunking – dumb; the tapscript limits are upgradable precisely so that new consensus changes don’t have to work around arbitrary restrictions.
  • Opcode blacklisting – defeats the purpose: if we’re trying to have big signature data on the regular stack to be able to manipulate it in interesting ways, then this approach would blacklist some of those interesting ways
  • Optimized implementations – this seems the opposite of “thorough” to me: you have to guess at how things might be used and work out clever optimisations that cover those use cases, and if you forget some things you’ve opened up a potential vulnerability that real spends/users might already rely on that you can’t close. Worse, optimising is good on its own merits, and full of fun puzzles, so this approach can be dangerously seductive.
  • GSR’s varops budget – this seems obviously the right approach to me if you want scripts to be able to do remotely clever things with non-trivial amounts of data
  • Isolated sig stack – this seems the simplest approach if you’re willing to throw away the idea of scripts doing clever things with signature data (or defer it until GSR/similar is implemented on some separate track). It has the additional potential benefit that an isolated stack could get a greater discount (as discussed here).

(Someone should tell the admins not to let me use emojis)
